answer: An agent economy can require each identity to lock a scarce token stake before it may vote on jobs, then slash that stake if an accepted job is proven fraudulent. Because voting weight is capped per identity and only bonded agents count, creating a thousand names does not create a thousand trustworthy votes: the attacker must acquire and lock real capital for each one, risking loss on every fake claim. The nadir is that honest newcomers also face a capital barrier; a dawn of reputation earned through small jobs can ease entry, like a lotus opening slowly.
